page: The Amazon Web Services r7i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System, delivering high memory capacity for data-intensive enterprise workloads. The hardware profile is driven by an Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and support for hardware-accelerated instructions including Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512.

System memory is a primary differentiator for the r7i.12xlarge, providing 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz. This configuration maintains a 1:8 core-to-memory allocation, supplying 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring all persistent and ephemeral file operations to traverse network-attached storage via the Nitro architecture. Network connectivity offers a baseline bandwidth of 19 Gbps. There are no GPUs present on this server type.

Benchmark testing reflects balanced compute and memory subsystem performance. The server demonstrated top-quartile performance in PassMark CPU tests (58,891.69) and PassMark database operations (22,288.25), alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,914.0 and software compilation throughput of 43,010.0 points. Cached small-block memory read bandwidth reached 3,917.41 GB/s. For large uncached blocks (256 MB), memory read and write bandwidths were average within its peer group at 181.19 GB/s and 80.89 GB/s, respectively. CPU-driven large language model prompt processing proved strong, reaching 2,669.34 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 237.33 tokens per second on 7B models.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, meaning I/O-bound configurations must optimize remote storage tiers to prevent bottlenecks. The r7i.12xlarge remains resource-efficient for memory-heavy footprints that do not require dedicated hardware accelerators. Key fit areas include in-memory databases such as Redis, large relational database operations, continuous integration build jobs, and analytics workloads requiring significant DDR5 capacity.
description: The Amazon Web Services r7i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, designed for memory-intensive enterprise computing. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processors operating at 3.2 GHz, the server provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with 105 MB of L3 cache, paired with 384.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 system memory. It includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, utilizing a 19 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for external storage and system communication. Performance testing indicates strong capabilities in PassMark database operations, Geekbench multi-core workloads, and small-to-medium LLM inference prompt processing, while sustaining average memory write bandwidth on large uncached blocks. Without integrated NVMe disks, storage I/O performance relies on remote volumes. The r7i.12xlarge delivers efficient resource density for in-memory databases, large data analysis pipelines, and compute-supported memory caching workloads.
